does: Turns source material into a quiz that checks whether somebody understood it: the concepts it will test, named and shown for approval first, then the questions, each one carrying the place in the source it came from and the place to go back to.

offerings.name: Make a quiz
offerings.does: Turns source material into a quiz that checks whether somebody understood it, staged at an address they can open.

inputs.name: site read
inputs.description: What site-reader read, its site-read.json. Each page is a source of its own with its own credit and address, and every part is placed at its page, so a question cites where its answer came from. An article read is quizzed on the article and not on the pages it links to.

inputs.name: audience
inputs.description: Who the quiz is for and what they already know. It can be given as the AUDIENCE setting or as an "audience: ..." line in the message, and an audience given either way, or settled by the source, is always used. In an unattended run with no audience given, the default is "a general reader meeting this subject for the first time".

inputs.name: how many questions
inputs.description: How many questions to write. It can be given as the HOW_MANY setting, as a "how many: 5" line in the message, or in the message's words ("make 5 questions"), and the run context's answer is read when neither gives one.

steps.name: Read the source
steps.does: Reads every source given into one text with a place name on every part, so a question can cite where its answer lives.

steps.name: Name the concepts
steps.does: Names what the material actually teaches this audience, as the list the questions will be written from.

steps.name: Write the questions
steps.does: Writes the questions from the concept list, each one testing whether the person understood rather than whether they remember the wording.

steps.name: Check the questions
steps.does: Refuses the faults that make a quiz wrong, and the faults that make it test reading rather than knowing.

steps.name: Stage the quiz
steps.does: Places the quiz as a page somebody can open and take, marked in their own browser.

inputs.description: Who the quiz is for and what they already know. It can be given as the AUDIENCE setting or as an "audience: ..." line in the message, and an audience given either way, or settled by the source, is always used. In an unattended run with no audience given, the default is "a general reader meeting this subject for the first time".

refusals:
Asking about anything the source did not say. Every question names the place in the source its answer came from, and a question that cannot name one is not written.
Writing a quiz when the source settles no audience and none was given, except in an unattended run, where it writes for the default audience, "a general reader meeting this subject for the first time", and the reply says plainly that this audience was assumed. Questions for a new hire and questions for an expert are different questions, and a quiz averaged across both is useless to either.
Recording who answered or what they scored. The quiz is marked in the person's own browser, and nothing is sent anywhere or kept.
Marking a person. It writes the answer a person should be able to give; it does not grade the one they wrote.
Using the tricks that test reading rather than knowing: a right answer that is the longest choice, two choices that mean the same thing, a choice reading all of the above, and stacked negation.
Publishing anywhere but the quiz address. Putting the quiz in front of anybody is the person's decision.
escalates: A source that settles no audience goes back to the person as that one question, with no quiz written, except in an unattended run, where the default audience, "a general reader meeting this subject for the first time", is used, the job goes on, and the reply says plainly that this audience was assumed and that a different audience can be asked for.

The concept list goes to the person before any question is written, and their answer is what the questions are written from. In an attended run the job stops once the concepts are named and sends the list back as its question; the person's reply in the job's thread (a yes, the list edited, or a change in their own words) is what the questions are written from, and a change in words is written into the list and shown again. A concept list sent with the request is that answer already. In an unattended run nobody is there to answer, so the list is named, delivered beside the quiz, and the job goes on.
A source that contradicts itself on a fact a question would test goes back with both readings named, for the person to choose.

records.name: the source as received, per job
the reading, with the place name on every part
the concept list per job as approved
the quiz per job as delivered
the coverage check per job: every concept, and for each the questions that test it or the reason it was left
the signed job manifest of each delivery, listing each piece by the step that made it. The adapter signs it from pieces.json and keeps it beside the reply.
every call to the text-reasoning service for a job: how many were made, the ceiling they were made under, which model made them, the step that was running and, where the job stopped, what stopped it
what this job did not have and did anyway: each thing that was missing, what was done instead, and the reason where it is known

systems.name: text-reasoning
systems.needs: to name the concepts the material teaches and write the questions that test them, which are the two judgments in this job

systems.name: source-host
systems.needs: to open a page address the person gave and read its text; the address must open without a sign-in, and a credential pasted into a message is refused

systems.name: draft-host
systems.needs: to place the quiz page and the quiz file where the person can open them

can_use.does: builds the quiz page in the brand's ground and ink rather than this agent's, colors the title, the links back and the buttons where the brand states those, takes its accent for the rest, sets the title in the brand's heading face at the weight it asks for and everything else in its body face, checks the page it built against the contrast the brand requires and says plainly when the brand's own colors do not reach it, and keeps every right and missed verdict paired with a word and a glyph
